annotations.text:
Lido, redrawn for iOS 26.

Every piece of chrome is Liquid Glass and floats: nav is a set of glass capsules rather than a bar, the trip panel is a glass slab overlapping its cover, and the composer and dock sit above content that visibly passes under them. Two variants are used consistently — regular glass over content, clear glass over a cover with a scrim beneath it for legibility. Corner radii are concentric: a 30px panel holds 18px tiles at 16px inset.

The structural move underneath: a trip's four tabs (Overview / Packing / To-Do / Food) become one scrollable trip page with module cards, so outstanding work is visible without hunting.

References: Luma for the event page, ChatGPT for the composer and suggestion chips, Wabi for the floating dock and warm card ground, Family/Canopi for the trip-first home.

The kit

Glass needs something behind it, so the covers do real work: full-bleed art at the top of Home and Trip, an ambient colour wash on the list screens, and a blurred backdrop under the New trip sheet.

On photos — Unsplash is blocked by this session's network policy (403 on images.unsplash.com, unsplash.com and plus.unsplash.com), and the artifact CSP blocks external images regardless, so a photo has to be embedded rather than linked. The covers here are drawn instead: layered riso poster art with sun, sea, headland and terraced houses. Give me image files and I will inline them; the layouts take a photo unchanged.

Two directions I did not take, sketched so you can push back. These are pre-glass wireframes — they are about structure, not surface.

Option B treats the trip as an operations board — fastest to answer "what do I owe the group?", but it reads like a task app. Option C treats it as a loose board of cards you arrange — feels like the holiday, but it is hard to scan and expensive to build. The Screens page sits between them, leaning toward B's clarity with C's warmth.
